relevance_note: Family study of a Mexican proband with an LCAT variant: 'The proband was found homozygous for a previously reported LCAT gene mutation (Thr37Met). A sister and two sons of the proband were heterozygous for the same mutation.'
method_note: Read the paper in full; a short Python script assembled the JSON and cut table spans from Tables II-IV (patients as columns; column order II-1, II-3, II-4, II-5, II-6 [Proband], II-7, III-2, III-3, III-4 as in the 'ID subject' header row); script cell values were checked against the tables by eye. All nine family members are in scope (proband II-6, three heterozygous relatives II-7, III-3, III-4, and five tested wild-type relatives II-1, II-3, II-4, II-5, III-2); wild-type relatives have no variant rows. The proband's label is II-6 (Table II header 'Proband ... II-6'); the converted headers of Tables III and IV repeat 'Proband -' over every column (conversion artifact). Variant values are written with '>' where the Markdown has '>' (spans keep '>'). Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: Discussion gives the mutation as 'c.110T in exon 1' and the Fig. 3 legend as 'Thr13Met', against 'c.110C>T' and 'Thr37Met' elsewhere; the Results call it 'substitution of threonine for methionine' while writing Thr37Met. Table '-' and '+' symbols (corneal opacity, diabetes, carotid plaque) are not defined in any legend, so '-' cells were not used to exclude anything; corneal opacity for relatives is therefore not reported. Table IV '-' for the proband's CAC and for II-7/III-2 cIMT/CAC are taken as not measured/not reported. CAC score 0 (II-1, II-3, II-5, III-4) recorded as coronary calcification excluded using the methods' definition (SA = CAC score >0) as second span. Carotid plaque excluded for the other relatives from 'present only in the proband and in the wild-type brother'. Low HDL-C marked observed for wild-type relatives from the authors' group statement 'low in non-carriers of the mutation' (relative to healthy controls; II-4 has 51 mg/dl). Inheritance 'inherited paternal' for III-3 and III-4 because their father (the proband) is stated to be homozygous; II-7's parents were not tested. 'normal renal function' was used to exclude 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure' for the proband. Lab values in tables were not interpreted as abnormal unless the text says so. Publication year is not printed (only Received 2013 / Accepted 2014), so year is null.
